$schema.description: Path or URL of the JSON Schema for editor autocomplete and docs.

guestWorkspace.description: Where the workspace appears inside the sandbox. "auto" = C:\Workspace\<folder name>. "mirror" = the same path as on this PC, so absolute paths in configs and build caches match (another drive letter such as F: is a subst drive onto C:\Mirror\F); paths the sandbox reserves (C:\Users\..., C:\Program Files\...) fall back to "auto".

enabled.description: Keep what your .gitignore lists (.env files, node_modules, build output ...) out of the sandbox. The sandbox works on a copy of the project without those files, kept in step with it both ways within about a second; what it creates that is ignored (its own node_modules, builds) stays in the sandbox. Git works as usual. Off = the project folder itself is mapped.

exclude.description: Also keep these out, as .gitignore patterns, e.g. secrets/, *.pem, data/private/.

host.description: Folder on this PC (relative paths are relative to the config file).

guest.description: Where it appears inside the sandbox, e.g. C:\Assets, or on another drive letter (D: to Z:) such as F:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Game (shown as F: at boot). Leave it out to use the same path as on this PC (a folder inside the project stays where it is in the project). A full path only; one the sandbox cannot use (C:\Windows\..., C:\Users\..., one already in use) stops the launch with the fix.

readOnly.description: true = the agent can only read it.

optional.description: true = skip it quietly when the host folder does not exist.

mappings.description: Extra folders (relative paths are relative to this file), e.g. a read-only data folder at another place in the sandbox. Folders outside the project are used only as your projects.allowOutsideMappings setting allows (by default you are asked once).

scripts.description: Scripts (.ps1 / .mjs / .cmd, relative to this file) run inside the sandbox before the agent.

memoryMb.description: Sandbox RAM in MB (>= 2048), or "auto": free RAM minus reserveHostMb, capped at maxMemoryMb. Never more than this PC can keep in RAM for it (its RAM minus the larger of reserveHostMb and 25 %, 2 GB more with vGPU): a bigger value is lowered.

maxMemoryPercent.description: memoryMb "auto" never takes more than this share of this PC's total RAM (percent).

reserveHostMb.description: Memory always left for this PC when memoryMb is "auto": the sandbox gets at most (free RAM, and RAM plus paging file still unused) minus this.

vGpu.description: Virtual GPU. Off by default: Microsoft notes it widens the sandbox attack surface. The sandbox then uses this PC's graphics card, and with some graphics drivers heavy use can freeze the whole PC: turn it on only when a program in the sandbox needs the GPU (the mesa toolchain gives software OpenGL without it).

networking.description: Internet access. false is the only hard network isolation Windows Sandbox offers.

clipboard.description: Shared clipboard between this PC and the sandbox. Also lets an agent's copy (in sandbox attach) reach this PC's clipboard.

protectedClient.description: Run the sandbox window in Protected Client mode (recommended).

headless.description: Hide the sandbox window (sbx-show brings it back). A headless sandbox shuts down when its last session ends.

keepAwake.description: Keep this PC from sleeping while a sandbox runs, so agents left working overnight keep going (the screen may still turn off; closing a laptop lid still sleeps it).

blockPrivateRanges.description: Block your LAN (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, SMB) from inside the sandbox.

blockHosts.description: Never reachable from the sandbox, e.g. production servers or telemetry (each exact name; the sandbox's hosts file sends them nowhere).

killSwitch.description: Block all traffic that does not go through the tunnel: when the tunnel cannot start, the sandbox stays offline instead of using your normal connection. A project can only turn this on, never off.

copyFromHost.description: Copy Node, Git, nvm and the agent from this PC when they are installed here.

fallbackToInstall.description: Download anything that cannot be copied from this PC.

refresh.description: Re-copy / re-download everything on the next launch.

enabled.description: Provide Git for Windows (and Git Bash, which Claude Code needs).

access.description: full: normal git. readonly: status/log/diff/show/blame only (no commit, push, checkout, ...). none: no git at all; .git is hidden from the agent.

enabled.description: Windows Terminal as the sandbox window.

requireChecksum.description: Refuse any toolchain, database or tool download that has no published checksum (SHA-256/SHA-512) to verify it against. false = allow those, as before. Downloads that do have a published checksum are always verified. A project's .sandbox-config.json can only turn this on.

version.description: Default Node version for nvm. "host" = the Node on this PC. A project's .nvmrc / .node-version wins.

extraVersions.description: More Node versions to install (switch with nvm use). On top of the up to 3 versions copied from this PC's nvm, not counted towards that limit.

corepack.description: pnpm and yarn through corepack (a project's "packageManager" in package.json picks the version).

volta.description: Volta: true, false, or "auto" = when the project's package.json has "volta" pins or this PC uses Volta. With pins, Volta's node/npm/yarn/pnpm come first on PATH.

globalPackages.description: npm packages installed globally into the default Node version, installed once and kept (e.g. ["typescript", "npm-check-updates"]).

enabled.description: Python 3 (CPython with pip). true, false, or "auto" = only when the project has pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, setup.py, Pipfile or .python-version.

version.description: Python 3 version prefix, e.g. "3" or "3.12". A project's .python-version wins.

python2.description: Also install Python 2.7 as python2 / pip2.

pyenv.description: pyenv-win (pyenv install / local / global): true, false, or "auto" = when this PC uses pyenv. .python-version is honoured either way, and `uv python install` always works.

tools.description: Python command-line tools installed with `uv tool install` (needs uv), installed once and kept (e.g. ["poetry", "ruff", "pre-commit"]).

enabled.description: Rust via rustup (cargo, rustc). true, false, or "auto" = only when the project has Cargo.toml or rust-toolchain(.toml).

toolchain.description: Default toolchain, e.g. "stable". rust-toolchain.toml in a project wins.

host.description: Host triple, or "auto": x86_64-pc-windows-msvc when the MSVC toolchain is on (like most PCs), else x86_64-pc-windows-gnu (MinGW is its linker).

components.description: Extra rustup components, installed once and kept (e.g. ["rust-src", "llvm-tools"]).

targets.description: Extra rustup targets, installed once and kept (e.g. ["wasm32-unknown-unknown"]).

crates.description: Binaries for cargo: prebuilt via cargo-binstall when the crate publishes a Windows build, else compiled with `cargo install --locked` (slow the first time), installed once and kept (e.g. ["sccache", "cargo-nextest", "cargo-deny"]).

targetDir.description: "shared": cargo's default target\ (shared with builds on this PC, so builds on either side invalidate the other), "separate": <workspace>\target\sandbox (kept, no cross-talk), "local": on the sandbox's own disk (fastest, lost every boot), or a guest path.

linker.description: GNU host: "lld" links with Rust's own lld through MinGW's gcc (much less memory than GNU ld), "gnu" with GNU ld.

linkSlots.description: GNU host: how many programs may link at the same time in the whole sandbox (other links wait). "auto" = one per 3 GB of sandbox memory after 6 GB, 2 to 8 (the memory governor slows links down too when memory runs short).

enabled.description: MSVC (cl, link) and the Windows SDK, portable from Microsoft's Visual Studio manifest (~1-2 GB once), with vcvars64.bat and vswhere. true, false, or "auto" = only when the project has a .vcxproj, CMakePresets.json, a script calling vcvars/vswhere, or a Rust project when this PC builds Rust with MSVC.

acceptLicense.description: Required to install MSVC: you accept the Visual Studio licence terms (https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/license-terms/), which need a Visual Studio licence.

msvcVersion.description: "latest" or an MSVC tools version prefix, e.g. "14.44".

sdkVersion.description: "latest" or a Windows SDK build, e.g. "26100" or "10.0.22621".

enabled.description: MinGW-w64 GCC with CMake, Ninja, premake5 and mingw32-make (also Rust's linker). true, false, or "auto" = only when the project has CMakeLists.txt, Makefile, meson.build, premake5.lua or Cargo.toml.

flexBison.description: win_flex / win_bison, the parser generators many C/C++ projects (game engines among them) need; CMake finds them.

enabled.description: .NET SDK (C#, F#). true, false, or "auto" = only when the project has a .sln, .slnx, .csproj, .fsproj or global.json.

channels.description: SDK channels, e.g. ["LTS", "8.0"]. A project's global.json is installed too.

tools.description: Global .NET tools (`dotnet tool install -g`), installed once and kept (e.g. ["dotnet-ef", "csharpier"]).

workloads.description: SDK workloads (`dotnet workload install`), installed once and kept (e.g. ["aspire", "wasm-tools"]).

frameworkTargets.description: .NET Framework reference assemblies (targeting packs) from NuGet, so net4x and old-style .csproj projects build without Visual Studio, e.g. ["net48", "net472", "net462"]. The 4.8 runtime itself ships with Windows.

netfx35.description: .NET Framework 3.5 runtime (a Windows feature, enabled from Windows Update on every boot; a few minutes).

enabled.description: Go. true, false, or "auto" = only when the project has go.mod or go.work.

version.description: "stable" or a version prefix such as "1.23". A go.mod asking for newer fetches it itself (GOTOOLCHAIN=auto).

tools.description: Go tools (`go install <path>@<version>`), installed once and kept (e.g. ["golang.org/x/tools/gopls@latest"]).

enabled.description: Java: Eclipse Temurin JDK. true, false, or "auto" = only when the project has pom.xml, build.gradle(.kts), settings.gradle(.kts), mvnw, gradlew or .java-version.

version.description: "lts" (newest LTS) or a major version such as "21". A project's .java-version or .sdkmanrc wins.

maven.description: Apache Maven (mvn). A project's mvnw works either way.

gradle.description: Gradle (gradle). A project's gradlew works either way.

enabled.description: Ruby (RubyInstaller, with gem and bundler). Gems with C extensions need MSYS2, which is not included. true, false, or "auto" = only when the project has Gemfile, a .gemspec or .ruby-version.

version.description: Version prefix, e.g. "3" or "3.3". A project's .ruby-version wins.

gems.description: Gems installed globally, installed once and kept (e.g. ["rubocop"]).

enabled.description: PHP (with the Visual C++ runtime it needs, installed on every boot). true, false, or "auto" = only when the project has composer.json, artisan or .php-version.

version.description: Version prefix, e.g. "8" or "8.3". A project's .php-version wins.

enabled.description: Deno. true, false, or "auto" = only when the project has deno.json, deno.jsonc or deno.lock.

PowerShell 7 (pwsh), portable (~110 MB once); `powershell` stays Windows PowerShell 5.1. true, false, or "auto" = when a .ps1 at the root or one folder down has #Requires -Version 7 / -PSEdition Core or a `pwsh ...` usage line, or, in a folder that is no project yet, when this PC has PowerShell 7.

gh.description: GitHub CLI (gh). Only with provisioning.git.access "full": gh can push and merge through the GitHub API, past a read-only git. Your PC's gh login is never copied; `gh auth login` inside persists (GH_CONFIG_DIR), unless a token you saved for sandboxes is handed over (github.shareToken). "auto" = when the project has a .github folder.

zstd.description: Zstandard (zstd). "auto" = off; set true to get it.

openssl.description: `openssl` on PATH, from the copy Git for Windows ships (its mingw64\bin is not put on PATH, so it cannot shadow MinGW's gcc). "auto" = on.

enabled.description: Bun (JavaScript runtime and package manager; claude-mem needs it). true, false, or "auto" = only when the project has bun.lock, bun.lockb or bunfig.toml.

uv (fast Python package and tool manager; claude-mem needs it for its search index). true, false, or "auto" = only when the project has uv.lock, a [tool.uv] pyproject.toml, toolchains.python.tools, or an agent installed with uv.
Microsoft Visual C++ runtime for tools that need it (a real installer, so it runs on every boot, ~15 s). PHP installs it regardless.
Mesa 3D (llvmpipe): OpenGL 4.5 in software for games and apps when there is no GPU (sandbox.vGpu off). Copy opengl32.dll and libgallium_wgl.dll from %MESA_DIR% next to the program's .exe.

vulkan.description: Also software Vulkan 1.4 (Mesa lavapipe) with the Khronos loader, registered for every program; for wgpu set WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan.

enabled.description: Portable VS Code inside the sandbox (code on PATH, desktop shortcut); its settings and extensions persist. true, false, or "auto" = when VS Code is installed on this PC.

setup.description: Point VS Code at the sandbox's own tools (JDK, Python, Go, compilers, .NET, Git, PowerShell 7 and Git Bash terminals) and install the language extensions for the toolchains in use.

recommended.description: Also install the extensions a project recommends in its .vscode/extensions.json.

extensions.description: More extensions to install in every sandbox, e.g. eamodio.gitlens, ms-azuretools.vscode-docker.

environment.description: Extra environment variables for the agent and every terminal, e.g. registry mirrors: {"NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY": "https://...", "PIP_INDEX_URL": "https://..."}.

enabled.description: PostgreSQL (with psql, pg_dump). User postgres, no password, localhost only: true, false, or "auto" = only when the project needs it (found from compose files, dependencies of every language, Prisma/ORM config and connection strings).

version.description: "latest" or a major version such as "16". A compose file pinning postgres:<major> wins.

enabled.description: MySQL-compatible database (MariaDB). User root, no password, localhost only: true, false, or "auto" = only when the project needs it (found from compose files, dependencies of every language, Prisma/ORM config and connection strings).

version.description: "lts" (newest MariaDB LTS) or a MariaDB series such as "11.4".

enabled.description: MongoDB with mongosh, localhost only: true, false, or "auto" = only when the project needs it (found from compose files, dependencies of every language, Prisma/ORM config and connection strings).

version.description: "latest" or a version prefix such as "8.0".

enabled.description: Redis (community Windows build), localhost only: true, false, or "auto" = only when the project needs it (found from compose files, dependencies of every language, Prisma/ORM config and connection strings).

DynamoDB Local (Amazon's official emulator, on the Java toolchain) with dynamodb-admin, a web UI to browse and edit tables: true, false, or "auto" = only when the project needs it (found from compose files, dependencies of every language, Prisma/ORM config and connection strings).

port.description: DynamoDB endpoint port inside the sandbox (http://localhost:<port>).

adminPort.description: dynamodb-admin web UI port (open http://localhost:<adminPort> in the sandbox's browser).

admin.description: Run dynamodb-admin next to DynamoDB Local.

enabled.description: SQL Server. It cannot run inside Windows Sandbox; when a project needs it you get a note to use Postgres or SQLite for local work: true, false, or "auto" = only when the project needs it (found from compose files, dependencies of every language, Prisma/ORM config and connection strings).
Allow sandbox claude --terminal / sandbox attach from this PC.

reuseSession.description: sandbox claude -t in a running sandbox reattaches to this folder's session when no terminal on this PC is attached to it (--new always starts another).

auto.description: Starting an agent attaches this terminal automatically, as if you passed -t (only in an interactive terminal).

autoHide.description: Hide the Windows Sandbox window whenever this terminal attaches; it keeps running (sandbox show brings it back).

confirmCtrlC.description: In an attached terminal and the sandbox window, a single Ctrl+C is held back (the title says so) and only a second one within 1.5 seconds reaches the agent: a Ctrl+C meant as "copy" no longer stops it. Esc still stops an agent.

enabled.description: Copy your desktop look into the sandbox.

install.description: Apps from the catalogue to install in every sandbox (the Apps screen in the menu lists them by category). Each is downloaded once and kept.

enabled.description: Copy selected Claude settings from this PC into the sandbox.

overwrite.description: Refresh these settings from this PC on every launch.

copyCredentials.description: Copy your Claude LOGIN into the sandbox. Prefer sandbox account instead.

syncHistory.description: Bring conversation history in, and sync new history back (path-translated).

syncClaudeMem.description: Bring claude-mem data into the sandbox (its settings and backups stay on this PC).
